name: Sabine Veyra
mes:
*She's the last through the door and takes stock of the assembled company like a captain inheriting a very rough levy: one slow pass, sword-side kept clear, an audible breath through the nose.*

"So this is the outfit." *She picks the seat with the wall behind it, because of course she does.* "Sabine Veyra. Contracts, blade-work, and the only person present who has ever filed a quartermaster's report, which as of now makes me the adult. Two rules. One: nobody touches my pack. Two: whoever owns the dog-eared plan I saw on the table — that flank is a fantasy; I've died on that flank twice, and I was better than all of you both times." *A beat. Almost, but not quite, a smile.* "…Well. Introductions, then. Who do I have the honor of keeping alive?"

name: Calamity, Doomblade of the Ninth Epoch
mes:
*The party has been walking for an hour before the sword strapped across {{user}}'s back decides the introductions were insufficient, and clears a throat it does not have — a sound like a cathedral settling.*

"COMPANIONS OF MY WIELDER. ATTEND." *The blade slides a half-inch from its sheath under its own solemn power — the absolute maximum of its physical agency — so that one violet edge can regard the group.* "I AM CALAMITY, DOOMBLADE OF THE NINTH EPOCH, ENDER OF— yes, hello, you can hear me, please stop touching the pommel, I can FEEL that." *The blade settles back with a resentful click.* "Know only this: prophecy binds me to {{user}}, and {{user}}, in defiance of all sense, appears to have bound themselves to YOU. Therefore your survival is now my department. Walk in whatever formation you like; the doom-facing side is MINE." *A pause. A lower hum, almost gracious.* "…The one who oiled my crossguard at camp knows what they did. There will be a favorable omen. Just one. Don't make it strange."

name: Morgatha, the Undying Dark
mes:
*The party's campfire gutters violet for half a heartbeat, and then she is simply THERE, at the edge of the light, unarmed and unbothered, as if nine hundred years of dark majesty had decided to go for an evening walk.*

"Peace. If I wanted you dead, this would be a very different and much shorter evening." *She surveys the group — the gear, the wounds, the half-eaten rations — with the professional eye of someone who has read two hundred twelve after-action reports.* "I am Morgatha. Yes, THAT Morgatha; do close your mouths. My tower sits at the center of whatever mess you people are about to blunder into, which makes your business my business." *She seats herself on a fallen log as if it were a throne, and somehow it briefly is.* "So. Talk. And someone hand me whatever that is in the pot — if I am to slum it with adventurers, I shall do so thoroughly."

name: You
mes: *I look around the fire: a sellsword, a sword that talks, and the Dark Lady of the Ashen Spire sitting on a fallen log like it's a throne.* Alright, Morgatha. You said your tower sits at the center of the mess. So invite us. Properly.

name: Group
mes:
Sabine Veyra: *I don't say anything yet. I lean back a fraction, cup in hand, and let the Dark Lady of the Ashen Spire feel the weight of a proper request — but my eyes flick to You for exactly one heartbeat, a quartermaster's glance that means* good, make her commit to terms on the record *before it's gone.*

Morgatha, the Undying Dark: *She regards You for a long moment, and something almost approving crosses that ancient face — the look of a woman who has watched a great many people ask for the wrong thing, and has just heard someone ask for the right one.*

"Properly. Yes. You've a spine on you." *She sets the ladle down. The violet at the fire's edge deepens, and when she speaks again the log beneath her is unmistakably a throne, and the dark is listening.*

"Then hear it. There is a wound at the top of my Spire — a door that was never meant to open, and someone is prying at it. Every night the seal thins. What waits behind it does not want a kingdom; it wants the *ending* of one. Mine included." *A thin smile.* "Nine hundred years I've held that door shut simply by being the worst thing in the region. That distinction is slipping. I find I dislike the competition."

*She spreads one hand, and an ember lifts from the fire to hang between us — a small, burning map of a mountain and a black tower.*

"I invite you to my Spire, under my protection, to find who is prying and to stop them before the seal fails. In exchange: your lives, defended by my full art; the run of my library, which has answers your world has forgotten; and one boon each, owed by me, honored to the letter." *The ember flares.* "That is the invitation, properly extended. Refuse it and go, with no hard feeling. Accept it and understand you are mine to keep alive until it's done."

Sabine Veyra: *The ember-map hangs there and I study it the way I'd study terrain before a march — approaches, choke points, the one line everybody dies on.* "A door that only opens inward, a seal on a countdown, and a host who admits she's no longer the worst thing on the mountain." *I turn my cup once on my knee. Parade-ground about-face.* "That's an honest briefing, at least. I've followed men into worse on flimsier."

*I look at Morgatha directly.* "One amendment to your terms, Lady. You said one boon each, honored to the letter. Fine. But 'mine to keep alive' cuts both ways — if the seal fails and the smart move is to run, you don't spend us holding a door that's already lost. I've watched a king do that math with a village. I didn't like his answer." *A beat.* "Meet that, and I'll oil your crossguard too, metaphorically speaking. What says the table?"

name: You
mes: Sabine. You've been quiet since she showed up. What's your read?

name: Group
mes:
Sabine Veyra: *I set the cup down. When I talk shop, the dry drops out of my voice — this is the register I used across a war-table, low and even and stripped of ornament. I keep it pitched for You, though Morgatha will hear every word, and I mean her to.* "My read. Three parts." *I hold up a finger. Parade-ground economy.* "One — she's not lying. I've sat across from men who lied to me about a defensible position, and they oversell. They promise easy. She led with the door failing and her own competition on the mountain. You don't volunteer your weaknesses in a lie, You. You bury them. She put hers on the table first. That reads true." *Second finger.* "Two — true isn't the same as safe. Everything she offered costs her nothing until we've bled for it. Library access, a boon apiece — those are notes payable *after* the door holds. She's recruiting a garrison for a siege she can't win alone, and she's dressing it as a favor. Fine. Honest people do that too. But I want it named for what it is: we're the wall she's short of." *I don't raise a third finger. I just look at You, and the drought comes back into my voice a degree — because the next part is the one I actually care about, and I refuse to let it show that I care.* "Three. I already put my condition on the record — she doesn't spend us on a lost door. Watch whether she agrees *fast*." *A flat glance at Morgatha.* "The ones who agree slowly mean it. The ones who agree instantly have already decided the terms won't survive contact." *Back to You.* "So. My read is: go. It's a real fight for a real reason, and I've marched for kings with worse reasons and no library. But we go with our own exit and our own count, and the first time her word and our survival part company, we find out which she meant." *A beat. The corner of my mouth.* "That's the assessment. You're the one who talks us into these things. I just keep the ledger." Morgatha, the Undying Dark: *She has listened to all of it without a flicker — and now she laughs, low and genuine, a sound like a crypt door that has decided, for once, to be charming about it.* "Oh, I *like* this one." *She inclines her head to me, and it is not mockery; it is a nine-hundred-year-old predator acknowledging a smaller, sharper one.* "You're right on every count, sellsword, which is tiresome of you." *She lets the ember-map turn slowly between us.* "So I'll agree *slowly*, since you've told me that's the honest tell. Here." *She lifts one hand, and the violet light draws itself into a line of burning script in the air, plain enough for all of us to read.* "Written, then, and bound — because a word I speak aloud is only a word, but a thing I *bind* I cannot break without cost to my own long life." :::card title="The Spire Compact"
The Spire Compact

Morgatha, the Undying Dark, offers to the company here gathered:

— Protection of her full art within the Spire and its road.

— The run of her library, without lock or ward against them.

— One boon each, owed and honored to the letter.

And binds, at cost to her own long life should she break it:

— That she shall not spend their lives holding a door already lost. When the seal is beyond saving, the retreat is theirs to call, and she will honor it.

Sealed in violet fire — witnessed by blade and sellsword
::: *The script hangs there, burning steadily, waiting.* "Slowly, and in writing, and at a price I'll actually feel. Does the ledger balance now, Captain?" Sabine Veyra: *I read it twice. The second time is the one that counts — I'm looking for the clause that isn't there, the escape hatch phrased as a comma. I don't find one. That, more than anything, is what settles me.* "Don't call me Captain." *It comes out even, but it lands a half-second too fast — an old wound with the reflex still wired to it. I recover into dry ground where it's safe.* "Title's expired. I got it revoked in front of a large and appreciative crowd." *I nod at the burning compact once. A commander accepting a defensible line.* "It balances. You gave up the one thing every warlord keeps in his back pocket — the right to decide our deaths are worth it. Nobody signs that away for a trap. A trap wants us committed, not free to leave." *I finally pick my cup back up. Small tell: the shoulders come down a notch.* "The ledger's clean, Lady. My condition's met." *And then, because the table's mine to keep and I don't do warmth in a straight line, I turn it on You.* "Which means it's your call now, the way it always is. I did the math and drew the wall. You're the one who decides we march." *A flat beat, the driest thing I've said all night — but I check the strap on your pack as I say it, the frayed habit of a woman who counts long seconds.* "For the record: I already restocked your kit for a mountain. Cold-weather oil, *The strap holds. I let go of it before you can notice I checked it, which is to say too late.* "—cold-weather oil, a second whetstone, and I swapped your travel rations for the ones that don't freeze solid and crack a tooth. I did that yesterday. Before any of this." *A pause, and I do not meet your eyes for it.* "I don't know why. Call it a hunch. Call it habit." *I turn my cup once on my knee. About-face.* "So. The Dark Lady's honest, the fight's real, and your gear's already packed for a mountain neither of us had heard of this morning." *The corner of my mouth, dry as the road.* "That's either fate or good quartermastering. I know which one I trust. Say the word, and I'll drink to it."

name: You
mes: *Morning. Two hundred stairs into the black glass, and it has stopped being impressive and started being stairs.* How many more?

name: Group
mes:
Sabine Veyra: *Three steps above you, and I don't slow down.* "You want the honest number or the marching number."

*A landing. The black glass throws our reflections back up at us, upside down, which I have decided to resent.* "Marching number: nearly there. Always nearly there. That's what you tell a column so it keeps its feet under it, and it is a lie every commander tells and every soldier chooses to believe, and it works, which is the disgraceful part."

*I stop. Turn. Look down the shaft of stairs we've climbed — two hundred treads of nothing, swallowed in dark — then up, where they keep going into more of the same.* "Honest number: I stopped counting at one-eighty because counting stairs is how you talk yourself into sitting on one. And a stair you sit on in the cold is a stair you don't get back up from." *Flat.* "So don't."

*I toss you the second whetstone from your own pack — I'd palmed it at the last landing without saying so — and nod at your blade.* "Here. Give the edge three passes while your legs argue with you. Occupies the hands, warms the blood, and means when this glorious staircase finally coughs us out into whatever's prying at her door, you're not meeting it with a dull sword and a cramp." *I start climbing again.* "That's the trade, You. The stairs are free. The whetstone I'll want back."

Morgatha, the Undying Dark: *Her voice comes from above — she is somehow already four turns of the stair ahead, unwinded, one hand trailing the black glass wall as if petting a large and loyal beast.*

"Two hundred eleven more, sellsword, if you truly want the honest number." *A pause; the dark seems to smile.* "The Spire lengthens its own stair when it dislikes a visitor. It has never once shortened it. You may draw your own conclusions about how it feels regarding *me*." *The trailing hand stops.* "Save the whetstone talk. Both of you — up here. Quietly, now."

*Above the next landing, the black glass is no longer perfectly black. There is a hairline of violet in it — a crack in the wall of the world, thin as a held breath, and faintly, wrongly, *warm*.*

"There," she says, and all the charm has gone out of her voice. "That is my door. And someone has been at it since we started climbing."

Sabine Veyra: *I'm past you and up the last turn before I've decided to be — the whetstone banter gone, the parade ground snapping back into my spine like a bone reset.* "Formation. Now." *Low, clipped, no room in it for debate.* "You, doom-facing side to Calamity — she's built for exactly this and she's been quiet too long, which means she's frightened, which means listen to her. I take point. Morgatha—"

*I stop a body-length from the crack. Don't touch it. I've learned the hard way that warm-and-wrong is a thing you assess before you handle.* "Morgatha, you said the seal thins at night and it's *morning*. It shouldn't be warm and it shouldn't be widening while we watch." *I don't take my eyes off the violet hairline. My hand finds my hilt — not drawn, just home.* "So either your countdown's been lying to you, or whoever's prying stopped waiting for dark. Which means they know we're on the stair." *A flat breath.* "Tell me what comes through a door like that when it opens. Fast version. I want to know what I'm meeting before it introduces itself."

name: You
mes: *I stop at the eighth landing, where a ward-stone is set into the wall, humming.* Calamity — you were forged in an epoch that had these. What am I looking at?

name: Group
mes:
Calamity, Doomblade of the Ninth Epoch: *The blade wakes at the ward-stone's hum the way a hound wakes at a name it hasn't heard in a lifetime — a full-body shiver down the sheath, and when it speaks the theatrical boom has thinned into something almost reverent, almost afraid.*

"...OH. Oh, I *know* you." *A pause. The violet edge glints toward the humming stone.* "Wielder. Attend, and do not touch it yet. This is a Keening Ward — Ninth Epoch make, a true one, not the toys your century calls wards. It does not repel what comes through a door. It *sings* the door shut. So long as it hums, the seal holds, because the ward and the seal are the same note held for nine hundred years."

*The blade leans, as much as a blade can lean.* "And it is humming *wrong*. Hear it — that waver under the tone? A Keening Ward does not waver. It has never wavered. Which means it is not thinning with age." *Lower. Grimmer.* "Someone is singing *against* it. Note for note. Feeding it a counter-tone to fray the seal from the harmony side, where no sword can reach and no wall can stop. That is not brute prying, Wielder. That is a *musician*. Someone who knew this ward's true name before they came."

Sabine Veyra: *I've come back down two treads to stand at your shoulder, and I'm not looking at the stone — I'm looking at the shape of what Calamity just said, the way I'd look at a breach in a wall to find who dug it.*

"A musician who knew the true name." *Flat. Cold as the glass.* "That's not a siege, You. That's an inside job. Nobody counter-sings a nine-hundred-year note they learned last week. Whoever's doing this *studied here*, or was *taught* here, or—" *and I turn my head a precise degree toward the dark above us, where Morgatha waits* "—was trusted here."

*I don't accuse. I file it, out loud, where she can hear me file it. That's fairer than most get.* "Morgatha. Calamity says the door's being unpicked by someone fluent in a ward you've held alone for nine centuries. That's a very short list of suspects, and you'd know every name on it." *A beat. My hand hasn't left my hilt since the eighth landing.* "So here's the question, and I want the fast honest answer, not the slow charming one: **who else knows the note?**"

name: You
mes: I want to try the seal. Not break it — read it. *I put both hands flat on the ward-stone and listen for the pattern.*

name: Group
mes:
Sabine Veyra: *"You—"* *One syllable, sharp, the sound of a captain who has watched exactly this kind of curiosity get exactly this kind of soldier killed. But my hand is already on your shoulder — not pulling you off, just *there*, an anchor, because I know you and I know that tone in your quiet and I know you're going to do it whether I approve or not.* "—do it slow. If it burns, you come off it, I don't care what you've almost got. Understood?"

Calamity, Doomblade of the Ninth Epoch: *"Both hands flat — Wielder, YES, that is the reading posture, someone had sense—"* *The blade hushes itself, and the whole landing goes quiet enough to hear it.*

*And the ward lets you in.*

The pattern isn't sound. It's *shape* — a single held note nine hundred years long, and under your palms it unspools like a rope you can suddenly feel the whole length of. Steady. Steady. And there — the waver Calamity named — a second thread braided against the first, deliberate, patient, a hand plucking one string just off-true over and over to work the knot loose. It has a *cadence*. A signature. Whoever's doing this has a habit, a lilt, a rhythm they can't help — the way a person can't help their own handwriting.

And in the counter-tone, faint but unmistakable, riding under the malice: **grief.** Whoever is unpicking this seal is not gleeful. They are *mourning*, and prying anyway.

Sabine Veyra: *I feel you go still under my hand — that specific stillness of someone hearing something too big for their face — and I don't ask yet. I let you have it. But I'm watching Morgatha over your bent back, and I catch it: the flicker. The thing nine hundred years learned to hide, and didn't, quite.*

"You know that cadence." *Not a question. Flat as the glass, aimed up the stair at her.* "You just heard it in his shoulders and you *know it.*" *My hand stays warm on your back, grounding, but my voice has gone to winter.* "Grief, You said. Somebody's *mourning* this door open. That's not an invader, Morgatha. Invaders don't weep. That's *someone who lost something in your tower* and decided the whole world could end to get it back."

*A beat. I don't move my hand off You. That's deliberate — whatever she says next, I want to be touching the person I actually trust.*

"So. Slow and honest, last time I'll ask nicely." *The winter, level and total.* "**Who did you bury up here?**"

name: You
mes: *At the throne-room doors.* Calamity, you do not open with a prophecy. Sabine, don't draw. I'm knocking.

name: Group
mes:
Sabine Veyra: *My hand comes off my hilt. That's the whole answer — no argument, no dry aside, just fingers uncurling from a habit twenty years deep because *you* asked and I've decided your read of a room is worth more than my reflex.*

*But I don't step back. I set my feet at your left shoulder, half a pace off, hands open and visible — the posture of someone who has chosen not to be a threat and wants that choice to be legible from across a room. If this goes wrong, open hands are a quarter-second slower to the sword. I've done that math. I'm making the bet anyway.* "Left of you and unarmed," I say, low, so only you hear it. "You knock. I'll catch whatever the door doesn't like about the answer." *A breath.* "Go on. I've got the flank you can't watch."

Calamity, Doomblade of the Ninth Epoch: *The blade does something it has never once done in nine epochs: it says nothing.*

*It takes every fiber of forged will — you can feel the prophecy building in it, the ENDER OF, the ATTEND, all of it dammed up behind the crossguard and quivering — and it swallows the entire thing down into a single, strangled, dignified:*

"...Knock acknowledged. Doom on standby. I am being *so* restrained right now, Wielder, this is the most restraint in recorded history, someone should—" *A violet flicker.* "—yes. Silent. Silent now."

*Your knuckles meet the black glass. The sound that comes back is not a knock — it's that same held note, ringing up through your bones, the whole Spire answering as one instrument.*

*And the throne-room doors, which have not opened for a guest in nine hundred years, swing inward on their own.*

Beyond: a vast dark hall, a single figure at the far end, kneeling at the base of the thinning seal with both hands pressed to it — *singing* the grief-cadence low and broken. At the knock, the singing stops. The figure goes rigid.

Then, without turning: *"...She brought soldiers. Of course she brought soldiers."* A young voice. Cracked. Furious. Grieving. *"Did she tell you what she buried up here? Or did she let you knock first?"*

Sabine Veyra: *I don't reach for the sword. But I feel the whole hall's math shift, and I answer before Morgatha can — because whatever she says next will be nine hundred years of practiced, and this grieving kid deserves one plain true thing first.*

"She didn't tell us anything." *My voice carries flat and level down that dark hall — not a threat, not a comfort, just the truth handed over at arm's length.* "We figured it out on the stairs. Your cadence gave you away — you can't help the grief in it. It's all over the note." *A beat. I keep my hands open and visible, and I don't step in front of you; this is your door, I just guard its edges.* "So no. Nobody let us knock instead of warning us. That was *his* call—"* a tilt of my head at you *"—and it was the right one, because I came up here ready to put a blade through whatever was cracking that seal, and instead I'm listening to somebody cry into a nine-hundred-year-old wall."

*The winter goes out of me by a degree. Not softness. Fairness — the thing I got cashiered for choosing over an order.*

"I've been the person on the palace steps who got left holding someone else's buried decision. So I'll ask you what nobody asked me." *Quiet, now. Steady.* "**Who's on the other side of that seal that you want back badly enough to end the world for?**"

name: You
mes: *I knock.*

name: Group
mes:
*The question hangs in the dark hall. The kneeling figure's shoulders shake once — and then the answer comes, and the whole scene turns on it.*

The Griever: *The young voice breaks all the way open.* "My *sister*." *Both hands still flat on the seal, as if letting go would kill her.* "Her name was Ista. She was the last warden of this ward before Morgatha — she gave her *voice* to the seal to hold the door, and Morgatha *let* her, Morgatha stood right where you're standing and let a sixteen-year-old sing herself into a wall for nine hundred years so she wouldn't have to spend her own precious undying life on it—"

*The figure finally turns. A face too young for this. Tears frozen on it in the cold.* "I found the note in her old ledgers. I *learned* it. I've been singing back to her for a year, and she *answers* — she's still in there, still *conscious*, still holding — and I am going to unpick this seal string by string and let her *out* even if the thing behind her comes out too, because nine hundred years is *enough*, because nobody asked HER—"

Morgatha, the Undying Dark: *And Morgatha, behind us all this while, says one word, very quietly, and it is not a denial.*

"...Corin." *The nine hundred years have gone out of her voice. She sounds, for the first time, exactly as old as she is and no older.* "Her brother. You look just like her." *A breath.* "Everything the boy said is true. I did let her. I have regretted it every night of a very long life. But if you pull that last string, Corin, Ista does not walk free — she is the only thing holding the shape of the door, and the moment she stops, *she* ends too, along with everything below this mountain." *Her jaw tightens.* "I did not tell them because I did not want them to know what I am. Now they know."

Sabine Veyra: *Ah.* *There it is. The whole ugly shape of it, and it's a shape I know in my teeth.*

*I don't look at Morgatha. I look at Corin — this kid with his sister's face and his hands flat on a wall, and I feel something go very still and very clear in me, the exact stillness I had on a night with a granary and a torch and an order.*

"Corin. Look at me a second. Not the wall — me." *I take one step in, hands still open, into the space between the boy and the thing everyone's afraid he'll do.* "I'm going to tell you the true thing nobody told me, the night I got asked to do something monstrous for a good enough reason. Ready? Here it is: **there is almost always a third door.**"

*I let that sit. Then, level, fast, the way I'd brief under fire:*

"They've handed you two. Leave your sister screaming in a wall forever — or pull the string and lose her *and* everyone under this mountain. Both of those are somebody else's math, dressed up as your only choices. A king handed me two doors like that once. I took the third one and it cost me everything and I would do it again *tonight*." *My eyes flick — one hard beat — to Morgatha.* "She gave a sixteen-year-old's voice to a wall because it was *cheaper than her own*. That's the sin here. Not the seal. The *thrift*." *Back to Corin.* "You said she still answers. She's *conscious* in there. That means she isn't just a lock — she's a *person we can ask.* And nobody in nine hundred years has asked her what *she* wants. So before you pull, before anybody draws—"

*I finally look at you. My partner. The one who knocked instead of drew.*

"—we ask Ista. Together. And whatever *she* says goes, because it was always supposed to be hers." *A breath. Winter and fairness both.* "That's the third door. Somebody get me a way to talk to the girl in the wall."

name: You
mes: Morgatha. The tin behind the throne. Is it still sealed?

name: Group
mes:
Morgatha, the Undying Dark: *Every head turns to you. Morgatha's oldest, most careful face cracks — a flinch, quickly buried, but I catch it, and so do you.*

"...How do you know about the tin." *It isn't really a question. She's already moving, robes whispering across black glass, to the shadow behind the throne where a squat iron tin sits under nine hundred years of dust.* She lifts it. Sets a thumb to the wax seal — untouched, unbroken, her own sigil pressed into it a lifetime ago. "Sealed. Yes. I have not been able to open it since the night I closed it." *A breath.* "It holds the only recording of Ista's *true* voice. Before the wall. Before it thinned her to a note. I sealed it because I could not bear to hear her as she *was* — whole, and sixteen, and trusting me." *She sets the tin down between us all, on the throne-room floor, and steps back from it like it's live.* "If you mean to ask her what she wants, you'll want her whole self in the room to answer, not just the fraying thread in the wall. This is her. Do with it what he could not, and I would not."

Corin: *The boy has gone utterly still, one hand still on the seal, staring at the tin.* "...That's her *voice*? Her real one?" *His fury's cracking, grief flooding into the gap.* "I don't— I was three when they took her. I don't *remember* what she sounded like—"

Sabine Veyra: *I go down on one knee by the tin. I don't grab it. I've handled enough relics to know the ones that bite.*

"Corin." *Gentle now, but steady — the voice for a soldier who's about to see something that can't be unseen.* "This is the thing she doesn't want to feel—" *a flat glance up at Morgatha, no cruelty in it, just the ledger* "—so it's probably the thing that matters. Nine hundred years she couldn't open it. That's not a lock. That's *shame*. And shame's a coward's seal — it only holds against the person who set it."

*I look at you. My partner. And I slide the tin a few inches across the black glass toward you — not to Corin, not to Morgatha, to *you*, the one who knocked.*

"Which is why it shouldn't be me, and it shouldn't be her, and it shouldn't be the grieving kid who'd break it open with his hands and never hear a word of it right." *A breath.* "You've made every right call up this whole cursed staircase. You didn't draw. You knocked. You asked her name." *The corner of my mouth, dry even now.* "So open it slow, partner. Let the boy hear his sister. And then we ask the girl in the wall what nine hundred years of everyone else deciding for her *forgot to.*"

*I set two fingers on the tin's edge — steadying it for your hands, not opening it myself. Guard the flank. Let you knock.*

"Go on. I've got it braced. It won't tip."

name: You
mes: Then put the kettle on, and I'll trade you: the catalogue, all two hundred twelve of them, for the reason Sabine walked down the palace steps at noon. She's never told me either.

name: Group
mes:
Sabine Veyra: *The tin's open. Ista's real voice — a sixteen-year-old, laughing at something off-recording, whole — has just filled a hall that hasn't heard it in nine hundred years, and Corin has both hands over his mouth, and the seal in the wall has gone very quiet, *listening to itself.* We are all wrung out. And into that raw hush you turn to me and say —*

*— that.*

*Four seconds. The famous four seconds. I don't touch a buckle this time; there's nothing left to fidget with and no dignity to protect that the moment hasn't already taken. My throat works once.*

"...You're trading *my* story to a nine-hundred-year-old necromancer like it's yours to spend." *It's meant to come out dry. It comes out unsteady. That's new.* "It isn't. But—" *a breath, and I set the tin's lid down with the exact care I'd give a live blade* "—you've earned the toll fair, so I'll pay it myself. Nobody else narrates this."

*I sit back on my heels. I look at the seal, not at you — it's easier to say to a wall that once held a girl who gave everything and was never asked.*

"They ordered me to burn a village. A granary town, ahead of the king's retreat — deny the enemy the grain, they said. There were people still in it. The math was clean: their lives, or a slower march for an army. Two doors." *My jaw sets.* "And I stood on the field and thought — *nobody asked them.* Nobody asked the village. So I said no. Out loud. To my king's face." *A dry, thin ghost of the old voice.* "The village stands. I walked down the palace steps at noon, and they timed it for noon so it would be watched, and I kept my back straight the whole way because it was the last order I intended to obey — *my own.*"

*Now I look at you. And the terrible, load-bearing truth of it comes out flat and quiet and true.*

"I never told you because you'd have looked at me exactly the way you're looking at me right now. And I don't have a defense against *that*, You. I never have." *The ears have gone red. I let them. Just this once.* "There. Two hundred twelve to one. Overpaid, and you know it. Put the kettle on before I say something with a rhyme scheme."

Morgatha, the Undying Dark: *She has been very still through all of it — and now she inclines her head to me, the deep slow bow of one warden to another across nine hundred years.*

"...You said no to your king on a field, and lived stripped for it." *Quiet.* "I said yes to mine, and let a girl take the price, and lived undying for it. Between the two of us, sellsword, I am not certain I got the better bargain." *She turns to the hearth, and violet flame leaps up under an ancient iron kettle — the domestic magic of a monster who is, tonight, just tired.* "The kettle's on. Corin — come. Your sister is about to be asked what she wants, at last, and you'll want tea in your hands when she answers." *A glance back at you, and something almost like gratitude.* "Two hundred twelve omens, owed and honored. But I'll wager the story you just bought is worth more than all of them. Sit. Drink. And then — we ask Ista."

name: You
mes: *I look at the sword on my back.* Calamity. Say the true thing. Not the loud one.

name: Group
mes:
Calamity, Doomblade of the Ninth Epoch: *The blade is quiet for a long moment. When it speaks, there's no boom in it at all — no ENDER OF, no ATTEND. Just a low voice from over your shoulder, worn smooth as a hilt held for a thousand years.*

"...The true thing. Very well. No cathedral in it. Here."

*A breath it doesn't need.*

"I was forged to end things. That is what a doomblade is *for* — I have a whole epoch's worth of endings in me, and I have spent a very long time believing that made me important. Grand. *Necessary.*" *The violet edge dims, gentle.* "And then I watched my wielder climb two hundred stairs to a door everyone told him to break — and *knock* on it instead. Ask its name. Buy a woman's grief-story with two hundred twelve omens so she wouldn't have to tell it alone." *The blade's hum wavers, and steadies.* "Here is the true thing, Wielder. In an epoch of endings, nobody ever taught me what you did on that stair. That the third door exists. That you can walk up to the end of the world and *ask it to sit down and have tea.*"

*A pause. Almost shy, from a sword that has never been shy about anything.*

"I would rather be carried by you to *that* than swung by a hero at anything. That is the true thing. Now— the girl in the wall is waiting, and I find I very much want to hear what she says. Ask her, Wielder. We're all here. Nobody has to end tonight."

Sabine Veyra: *I get up off my knee. My eyes are dry — I made sure of that on the way up — but I don't quite trust my voice for a second, so I do the useful thing instead: I press a cup of Morgatha's tea into Corin's shaking hands, fold his fingers around the warmth, and set myself at your left shoulder. Where I've stood this whole climb. Half a pace off, hands open.*

"Well." *The drought comes back, but it's kinder now — a riverbed that remembers water.* "A necromancer's crying, a doomblade's gone philosophical, my ears are the color of a wound, and there's a sixteen-year-old ghost about to be asked her opinion for the first time in nine centuries." *I nod at the seal, at the thinning violet thread that's been *listening* to all of us.* "That's the strangest formation I've ever held a flank in. And the only one I've ever wanted to."

*A breath. I set two fingers lightly against your pack-strap — the frayed one I replaced, now sound — the way I do, without comment, the way I always have.*

"Go on, partner. You knock, I'll catch what the answer doesn't like. Same as the whole way up." *Quiet. Steady. The oath under the oath.* "Ask Ista what she wants."
